previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with psoriatic arthritis on chronic immunosuppression was admitted two days after an anal fistulotomy for right submandibular swelling, erythema, and pain. Initial evaluation revealed sialadenitis with imaging showing fluid and gas near the gland, raising concern for early Ludwig’s angina. He was started on clindamycin, warm compresses, sialogogues, and gland expression by ENT. A repeat CT showed worsening of the infected sialocele but no abscess or airway compromise. His symptoms improved over the next two days, white count trended down, and he became afebrile and tolerating oral intake. Thrush noted on admission improved with clotrimazole and was discontinued at discharge. He was discharged home on oral clindamycin to complete a 10-day course, with follow-up arranged with ENT and instructions to resume his baseline immunosuppressive regimen after antibiotics.

Brief Hospital Course:

history of these headaches which he describes as chronic daily

has a history of positive tenderness on pressure over the 
greater occipital nerve region as well as over the temporal 
region. Patient was diagnosed with cerviogenic headache and 
myofascial pain, with question of his psoriatic arthritis 
affecting his cervical spine as part of
the etiology. Patient reports this headache has the same 
characteristics of prior headaches and unfortunately, he has as 
yet been unable to obtain humeria on an outpatient basis. No 
meningismus, fever or altered mental status to suggest

trauma or point tenderness. Patient transitioned from IV

rheumatology who felt that increasing the steroids would not be

and an occipital nerve block was done. Bilateral GONB and TPI to 
Bilateral splenius capitis and occipitalis with 14 cc 0.25% 
bupivicaine PF and 10 mg MPA without complications

humira as above and this appears to have been quite a
